audit.title: CCIP Directory - Testnet

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: The page opens with `# CCIP Directory` then `## Networks testnet (65)` — no self-contained sentence a model can lift. There is no statement like "Chainlink CCIP supports 65 testnet networks." Weak.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Clean hierarchy (1 H1, H3 cards, 0 level skips, 0 sections over 600 words per measured facts). Each chain card is a coherent chunk with lane/token counts. No comparison table, and most chains sit behind a "See more" control, hurting chunk exposure.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Strong for a directory — 37 numerals (e.g., "Arbitrum Sepolia — 29 lanes | 4 tokens", "65" networks, "7" tokens). Missing: no chain selectors, router addresses, or chain IDs in the rendered text (those live on detail pages).

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 23 links, all internal, 0 external/primary. No link to the CCIP concept page, chain-selector reference, or supported-networks spec from the body prose.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: No definition of "CCIP," "lane," or "CCIP Directory" anywhere in the visible content. Nothing verbatim-liftable.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Strong. Valid `DataCatalog` with 65 `Dataset` entries and URLs, `BreadcrumbList`, canonical URL, 12 OG + 9 Twitter tags. Note a freshness inconsistency: head `article:modified_time` is `2025-05-19` while JSON-LD `dateModified` is `2026-09-21`; reconcile these.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No code — appropriate for a directory index; not a defect in context, scored neutral.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Answers "which testnet chains does CCIP support" implicitly via the list, but no question-phrased heading, no intro, no "how do I use this." An engine must infer intent from card data.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Consistent, unambiguous chain/token naming aids entity resolution; the ceiling is low only because there is so little prose.

audit.summary: This is the CCIP testnet directory — an index of 65 supported testnet blockchains and 7 tokens, each card linking to a per-chain detail page. Its standout GEO strength is machine-readability: a valid `DataCatalog` JSON-LD block enumerating all 65 chains with names, descriptions, and URLs, plus `BreadcrumbList`, canonical, and complete OG/Twitter tags. Its biggest weakness is a near-total absence of liftable prose — 206 words, no definition of what CCIP or this directory is, and no answer-first sentence stating the totals — so a generative engine has structured data but no quotable natural-language claim to cite. The honest verdict: excellent as a machine-parseable dataset, thin as retrievable documentary prose; a small prose layer would materially raise citability.

recommendations.title: Add an answer-first intro paragraph under the H1
recommendations.where: Immediately below `# CCIP Directory`, before `## Networks testnet (65)`.
recommendations.issue: Page jumps straight from title to card grid; no liftable sentence.
recommendations.change: Add 2–3 sentences, e.g. "The CCIP Directory lists the 65 testnet blockchains supported by Chainlink CCIP as of 2026-09-21. Each network page provides its chain selector, router address, active lanes, and supported tokens. Testnet currently supports 7 tokens including LINK, USDC, and CCIP-BnM."
recommendations.why: Gives engines a self-contained, statistic-bearing sentence to quote for "what chains does CCIP support on testnet" — the page's core query.

recommendations.title: Ensure the full 65-chain list is server-rendered, not hidden behind "See more"
recommendations.where: `## Networks testnet (65)` grid (only ~14 chains appear in rendered markdown).
recommendations.issue: ~51 chains are only present in JSON-LD, not extractable body text.
recommendations.change: Render all cards in initial HTML (progressive disclosure via CSS, not conditional DOM); or add a plain comparison table (Chain | Chain selector | Lanes | Tokens).
recommendations.why: Engines that read visible text (not JSON-LD) currently miss most chains; a full table is the single highest-lift extraction structure here.

recommendations.title: Add a symptom/question-phrased heading
recommendations.where: Section heading for the network list.
recommendations.issue: `## Networks testnet (65)` is concept-titled, not query-shaped.
recommendations.change: Add or reword to "Which blockchains does CCIP support on testnet?" (keep the count).
recommendations.why: Matches how devs/agents actually query; question-phrased headings win retrieval that noun-phrase headings lose.

recommendations.title: Reconcile the last-updated signal and surface it visibly
recommendations.issue: Conflicting freshness dates; neither is shown in rendered content.
recommendations.change: Align both to the true update date and print "Last updated: YYYY-MM-DD" in the page body.
recommendations.why: Visible, consistent freshness is an E-E-A-T/trust signal engines reward for time-sensitive directory data.

recommendations.title: Add inline authoritative links from the intro prose
recommendations.issue: 0 external/canonical links in body; all navigation is card links.
recommendations.change: Link "Chainlink CCIP" to the CCIP concept/overview page and "chain selector" to the chain-selector reference.
recommendations.why: Anchors the directory to canonical definitions, raising credibility and enabling citation chains.

recommendations.title: Define "lane" and "token" once near first use
recommendations.where: Intro paragraph or a one-line legend above the grid.
recommendations.issue: "4 lanes | 1 token" appears with no definition of a lane.
recommendations.change: Add "A lane is a directional route between a source and destination chain."
recommendations.why: Supplies a crisp, liftable definition that engines can quote when explaining CCIP lane counts.

antiPatterns: Content-behind-interaction: the "See more" control hides ~51 of 65 chains from rendered text extraction (JSON-LD compensates only for schema-aware parsers).
No keyword stuffing, marketing fluff, or unresolved cross-references — clean on those.
offPageNotes: Directory data is dynamic (lane/token counts change); ensure the JSON-LD `dateModified` and any visible date are regenerated on each data refresh.
Consider listing this hub and its per-chain pages in `llms.txt`/sitemap so agents can crawl the full 65-chain set programmatically.

The CLI should pass raw `<head>` (it did here) — dates were verifiable; the "datePublished/dateModified absent" measured fact refers to article-schema fields, not the `DataCatalog` block, which does carry `dateModified`.
